({{FOTV|2|4}}) (or '''Yosemite elder''') is the leader of the [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite chapter]] of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== Despite her chapter's stated aversion to the techno-religious practices of other chapters, they are considered allies by [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] of the [[Knights of San Fernando]] (who uphold said practices), to the point of being included as prospective supporters for a civil war against the dominant [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth chapter]], which Quintus claims "only takes and gives nothing in return." Compared to her fellow elders from the [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]] and [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado]] chapters also invited by Quintus, McRae is particularly serious about the brewing civil war, personally expressing concern about the consequences of violating the [[Codex]] and pitting Brother against Brother. She is particularly strict about following the Codex, although she can be convinced to see it as open for "interpretation."{{FOTV|2|2}} While she prizes her Brothers, her patience has its limits: When the [[Coronado elder]] insulted her as a woman, she instantly clapped back, ready to feminize him with her combat knife. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== The Yosemite elder, as well as the Coronado chapter's elder and the [[Grand Canyon elder|Grand Canyon chapter's elder]], arrived at [[Area 51]] via [[Brotherhood airship|airship]] to meet with Elder Cleric Quintus and hear his overtures for a new "axis of power" in the Brotherhood. The Yosemite elder reacted sarcastically to Quintus' remark about uniting under a common banner, believing that Quintus' chapter would hold most of the power in their alliance. The Yosemite elder claims that most of the chapters have drifted away from each other, and expresses disapproval towards the religious overtones of Quintus' chapter, stating that the Yosemite chapter "doesn't go in for any of [that] shit." The Coronado elder then snarks that, as a woman, she would not be allowed to even talk in the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado chapter]], with the Grand Canyon elder laughing as Coronado followed up with a deliberate insult to her feminity. In response, Yosemite drew her knife and threatened Coronado with "carving him one". When the Grand Canyon and Coronado elders begin arguing, she shakes her head in disapproval until Quintus breaks up the argument. He dispels the other elders' skepticism by displaying crates of [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]]s, assuring them that, thanks to cold fusion technology, he can produce more than humanity could ever use, which would seem to guarantee their superior firepower over the Commonwealth. Won over by Quintus' display, the Yosemite elder states that fratricide within the Brotherhood of Steel is prohibited by the Codex, but then pledges her allegiance by suggesting that "the Codex is open... to interpretation." Soon after, the Yosemite elder and the other elders sit together watching a brawl between two [[Knight (TV series)|knights]] in power armor, as well as [[Maximus]]' duel to the death with a [[Coronado knight]] right afterwards. While the Coronado and Grand Canyon elders seemed to enjoy the fight, smoking cigars and throwing air punches, the Yosemite elder simply watched with a serious expression on her face. She remained seated when [[Xander Harkness]] arrived. ===[[The Profligate]]=== The arrival of Xander Harkness causes the Yosemite elder to lose faith in Quintus' rebellion, falling back on the clear chain of command as outlined in the Codex; she and one other member of her chapter hold a private meeting with Quintus and his [[clerics]] in their command room. When she calls him out for his rebellion, Quintus tries to win her back by invoking the name of [[Roger Maxson]] and the history of the Brotherhood, claiming that just as Maxson "chose God" when he rebelled against the United States government at [[Mariposa Military Base]] to start the Brotherhood, their own rebellion would also be divinely just. However, the Yosemite elder remains unconvinced, telling Quintus again that she does not believe in the "religious stuff." She then leaves with her aide.{{FOTV|2|3}} ===[[The Demon in the Snow]]=== Upon the return of the disguised Thaddeus, pretending to be [[Xander Harkness]], McRae finds the disguised ghoul in the Area 51 cafeteria. She tries to negotiate with him, reaffirming her chapter's allegiance to [[Arthur Maxson|Elder Arthur Maxson]] on the basis of ideological gaps between her and Quintus. Upon seeing the two talk, the Coronado elder approaches the pair assuming they are striking a deal. He makes the offer to hand over Quintus' head in return for 300 [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion cores]]. When McRae interjects and states that Yosemite will do it without asking for payment, as proof of loyalty, Coronado only scoffs at her, disdaining her attitude and explaining that this apparent unwillingness to behave like a mercenary in negotiations is why the Coronado chapter does not even permit women to serve in their ranks. She snipes back, threatening to stab him in the mouth if he keeps talking. Coronado insists, offering two squadrons of knights to commit to assassinating Quintus, prompting McRae to state that Yosemite did not come empty handed either and proclaim a readiness for war. The dispute causes Thaddeus to suffer a panic attack. While Coronado plays it off, stating that it is probably a coronary and suggests "Harkness" walks it off, McRae offers to lift the armor's visor to let the "paladin" take a breath of fresh air. Thaddeus recoils back, but before anything can happen, the [[Grand Canyon elder]] walks in, demanding explanation for the theft of the [[cold fusion]] device. Hostilities erupt immediately. As Coronado orders his knights to suit up and deploy, McRae makes good on her threat and stabs him through the mouth, slicing off his tongue, then using him as a meat shield against Grand Canyon who opens fire shortly after declaring how cool her action was. She then joins the fray and the point-blank shootout at the mess hall. ==Appearances== The Yosemite elder appears only {{in|FOTV}}. She is portrayed by [[Sisa Grey]]. {{FOTV appearances|10=202|11=203|12=204}} ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox characters FOTV}} [[Category:Fallout TV series human characters]] [[Category:Brotherhood of Steel characters]] [[ru:Старейшина_Йосемитского_Братства_Стали]]
